name: International Space Station
lede: A modular outpost in low Earth orbit — U.S., Russian, European, and Japanese rooms bolted to a truss, flying 400 km up at 28,000 km/h.
credit: Schematic station model for the planetarium — not NASA CAD.

modules.name: Unity
modules.function: First U.S. connecting node. Passage between Destiny, Quest, Tranquility, and the Russian segment.
modules.blurb: The first U.S. module. Six berthing ports make Unity the American hallway.

modules.name: Zarya
modules.function: Functional Cargo Block — first ISS element. Power and propulsion in the earliest assembly flights.
modules.blurb: The station’s first piece on orbit. Russian-built, U.S.-funded, still the bridge to Zvezda.

modules.name: Zvezda
modules.function: Russian service module — living quarters, life support, engines, and the main ROS control post.
modules.blurb: The Russian home. Sleep stations, a dining table, and the engines that still reboost the stack.

modules.name: Destiny
modules.function: Primary U.S. laboratory. Science racks, the window facing ram, and the station’s U.S. command and control hub.
modules.blurb: The American lab. International Standard Payload Racks line both walls — biology, materials, and Earth science.

modules.name: Harmony
modules.function: Utility hub for Columbus, Kibo, and the forward docking port. Crew Dragon berths on the ram PMA/IDA.
modules.blurb: The crew-quarters node. Four sleep stations and the hallway to Europe, Japan, and visiting vehicles.

modules.name: Columbus
modules.function: ESA laboratory on Harmony’s starboard port. Fluid physics, biology, and external payloads on the end cone.
modules.blurb: Europe’s lab. A short, dense cylinder of racks — Biolab, Fluid Science, and a window on the starboard sky.

modules.name: Kibo
modules.function: Largest single ISS module. Japanese Experiment Module with an airlock to the Exposed Facility.
modules.blurb: Japan’s big room. The widest lab on station, with an airlock that hands experiments out to the porch.

modules.name: Kibo Exposed Facility
modules.function: External porch for space-exposed experiments, reached through Kibo’s airlock.
modules.blurb: The Japanese porch. Instruments sit in vacuum, robot-arm reachable, looking into the wake.

modules.name: Tranquility
modules.function: Life-support node — ECLSS, exercise, Cupola, BEAM, and Bishop on its ports.
modules.blurb: Where the toilets, water recycler, and exercise gear live. Cupola hangs off the Earth-facing port.

modules.name: Cupola
modules.function: Seven-window observatory on Tranquility’s nadir port. Robotics workstation and the best Earth view on station.
modules.blurb: Six side windows and a 80-cm top pane. Crews fly Canadarm2 from here and watch weather crawl over continents.

modules.name: Quest
modules.function: U.S. EVA airlock. Crew lock plus equipment lock for U.S. spacesuits.
modules.blurb: The American front door for spacewalks. Suits live in the equipment lock; the crew lock cycles to vacuum.

modules.name: BEAM
modules.function: Expandable habitat demo, now a storage room on Tranquility’s aft port.
modules.blurb: An inflatable fabric can that held pressure for years. Today it is mostly bags and spare parts.

modules.name: Bishop
modules.function: Commercial airlock on Tranquility’s zenith port for deploying CubeSats and external payloads.
modules.blurb: Nanoracks’ airlock. Smallsats leave station through here instead of riding a visiting vehicle’s trunk.

modules.name: Rassvet
modules.function: Mini-Research Module 1 on Zarya’s nadir. Cargo, experiments, and a Soyuz/Progress docking port.
modules.blurb: A Russian docking room under Zarya. Soyuz often parks here; crew use it as extra stowage and a sleep nook.

modules.name: Poisk
modules.function: Mini-Research Module 2 on Zvezda’s zenith. Docking port and a Russian EVA airlock.
modules.blurb: The zenith docking ball on Zvezda. Another Soyuz parking spot and a Russian spacewalk hatch.

modules.name: Nauka
modules.function: Multipurpose Laboratory Module on Zvezda’s nadir. Russian science, life support, and Prichal below.
modules.blurb: The newest large Russian room. It arrived late, fired thrusters on its own, then settled in as a lab and node.

modules.name: Prichal
modules.function: Spherical docking node on Nauka’s nadir with multiple Soyuz/Progress ports.
modules.blurb: A ball of docking ports under Nauka. Visiting Russian vehicles fan out from here.

modules.name: IDA-2
modules.function: International Docking Adapter on Harmony’s ram port. Crew Dragon and future commercial vehicles.
modules.blurb: The front door. Crew Dragon noses in on IDA-2 after a 16-orbit chase.

modules.name: IDA-3
modules.function: Second IDA on Harmony’s zenith. Alternate commercial docking port.
modules.blurb: Backup nose. A second IDA so two commercial vehicles can be attached at once.

modules.name: S0 truss
modules.function: Center Integrated Truss Segment over Destiny. Power backbone and Mobile Transporter rails.
modules.blurb: The keel. Power and data run through S0 into the labs below.

modules.name: P1 truss
modules.function: Port inboard truss with thermal radiators.
modules.blurb: Port inboard spar. Radiators dump lab heat to space.

modules.name: S1 truss
modules.function: Starboard inboard truss with thermal radiators.
modules.blurb: Starboard twin to P1. More radiator area for the U.S. segment.

modules.name: P3/P4 truss
modules.function: Port solar alpha joint and inner port power truss.
modules.blurb: Where the port wings start. The alpha joint rolls the arrays to face the Sun.

modules.name: S3/S4 truss
modules.function: Starboard solar alpha joint and inner starboard power truss.
modules.blurb: Starboard alpha joint. Same job as P3 — keep the cells lit.

modules.name: P5/P6 truss
modules.function: Outboard port truss and solar array set. First arrays on station, later walked outboard.
modules.blurb: The far port tip. Early ISS power lived here before the wings walked out.

modules.name: S5/S6 truss
modules.function: Outboard starboard truss and solar array set — last big truss piece.
modules.blurb: The far starboard tip. Completing S6 finished the original power truss.

modules.name: P4 solar arrays
modules.function: Port inner photovoltaic blankets.
modules.blurb: Blue-black blankets that track the Sun. They are why the station looks like a flying kite.

modules.name: S4 solar arrays
modules.function: Starboard inner photovoltaic blankets.
modules.blurb: Matching starboard wings. Together the four sets make most of ISS electrical power.

modules.name: P6 solar arrays
modules.function: Outboard port photovoltaic blankets.
modules.blurb: The first arrays launched. Relocated to the port tip so they would not shadow the newer wings.

modules.name: S6 solar arrays
modules.function: Outboard starboard photovoltaic blankets.
modules.blurb: Last original wings. After S6, iROSA roll-out arrays added even more power.

modules.name: Canadarm2
modules.function: Space Station Remote Manipulator System. 17-meter arm that walks the truss and berths visiting vehicles.
modules.blurb: Canada’s arm. Operators in Cupola or Destiny walk it end-over-end to catch Dragons and move cargo.
